source.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales
source.authors: Shi-Kai Qiu; Zixi Chen; Hoang Phan; Qi Lei; Andrew Gordon Wilson

record.tranche_reason: The study measures compute-optimal tokens per parameter at several compute budgets, a different but related test of compute-optimal allocation. It does not fit the loss power laws in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior loss-scaling laws and reports optimizer-comparison loss and compute-efficiency results, but does not itself test whether held-out loss follows a power law or whether small-run loss fits extrapolate. Those cited findings are not rows. The compute-optimal TPP results in Table 5 are recorded below.
record.test_reason: Section H.5 applies Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 2 (fixed FLOPs, model size varied, parabola minimum) on FineWeb at three budgets (4e18, 2e19, 5e19 FLOPs) for Adam and Muon. It reports per-budget optimal tokens-per-parameter. The method and measure match an original source, though the scale is small (about 12x in compute) and the main topic is optimizers. This bears on V3 (stable compute-optimal split) and V7 (the split depends on setup, here optimizer, data and tuning). The rest of the paper concerns hyperparameter transfer and compute multipliers and fits no loss power law.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find optimal TPP of 9.6 for Adam and 7.4 for Muon on FineWeb using Hoffmann's Approach 2. They note the 1.3x ratio matches Muon's ~1.4x compute multiplier under an assumed Chinchilla-style loss form. They attribute Adam's gap from Hoffmann's 20 to FineWeb's higher quality and more extensive tuning, without testing either cause. They do not discuss the per-budget drift in Adam's TPP.
record.recipe_differences: Studies optimizer hyperparameter transfer and compute-optimal TPP using FineWeb and a fixed-FLOPs approach; it does not reproduce the original loss-law fitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimal TPP differs between Adam and Muon. The authors also identify dataset quality and hyperparameter tuning as possible reasons their Adam optimum differs from the earlier estimate.

fits_no_version.finding: Matrix-preconditioned optimizers (Muon, SOAP, Shampoo) give a roughly constant 1.4x compute multiplier over AdamW from 190M to 1.4B, but only with muP plus 1/width weight decay. Under standard parameterization the gain shrinks with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured optimizer speedups versus scale depend on hyperparameter-scaling rules.

record.problems: The relevant compute-optimal TPP results cover three model-size budgets on FineWeb and do not fit allocation power laws. The authors state that limited compute constrained the scale of their experiments. The reported table values have no uncertainty estimates; the paper gives a 0.1% final-loss noise-floor estimate for separate hyperparameter-transfer experiments.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute. A Chinchilla-style loss form is only assumed in an argument (H.5).
No extrapolation of small-run fits to larger runs.
Separate exponents for N and D against C were not fitted. There is no Kaplan-versus-Hoffmann comparison, and compute spans only about one order of magnitude.
Shape at fixed parameter count was not tested. The width and depth sweeps concern learning-rate transfer.
No other modalities or training regimes.

missing.what: Aggregate optimal TPP across budgets: Adam 9.6, Muon 7.4 (ratio 1.3), compared with Hoffmann's 20. These are the figures the authors headline.
FLOPs values of the three budgets (4e18, 2e19, 5e19) for the TPP rows.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the tranche from T2 to T1 because H.5 explicitly uses Hoffmann Approach 2 with the same TPP measure. Evidence is thin: three budgets spanning about 12x compute, no uncertainty, and parabola minima only. The paper is not an original source. The compute-multiplier results use log-log interpolation of Adam loss against compute but fit no power law.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss scaling in parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.

The study reports optimal tokens per parameter at three compute budgets, but does not fit power-law growth for parameter count and token count separately, or test the Kaplan-versus-Hoffmann exponent claims over several orders of magnitude.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details on loss at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes such as image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream-task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.

The study examines optimizer- and setup-dependent compute-optimal TPP, but does not fit exponents for held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute, compare parameter-counting conventions or fitting methods, or test whether loss curves bend away from power laws.

relationships.reason: Adam's optimal TPP drifts from 13.3 to 11.5 to 8.8 as compute grows, so the split is not constant even over about 12x compute (r1-r3). There are three points and no error bars.
relationships.display_finding: Optimal tokens per parameter fell from 13.3 to 11.5 to 8.8 across three budgets spanning about 12× compute.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r1-r3 show decreasing optimal TPP, qualifying Hoffmann-style equal growth within this range. This does not establish unstable allocation powers: stable unequal powers remain compatible with ratio drift, and no allocation exponents or TPP intervals are reported.

relationships.reason: Muon's optimal TPP is near-constant (6.6, 7.1, 7.3), consistent with N and D growing equally over this narrow range (r4-r6).
relationships.display_finding: Optimal token-to-parameter ratios were 6.6, 7.1, and 7.3, consistent with roughly equal parameter and token growth over the narrow range.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: r4-r6 give approximately constant TPP of 6.6, 7.1 and 7.3, consistent with approximately equal parameter and token growth over the tested range; separate allocation powers are not estimated.

relationships.condition: Adam vs Muon on FineWeb with extensive tuning
relationships.reason: The compute-optimal TPP depends on the optimizer, with aggregate Adam 9.6 vs Muon 7.4 (1.3x). Adam's 9.6 is far below Hoffmann's 20, which the authors attribute (untested) to data quality and tuning (r1-r6; aggregates from Fig. 13 text).
relationships.display_finding: Aggregate optimal tokens per parameter are 9.6 for Adam versus 7.4 for Muon, a 1.3-fold difference, and Adam's ratio is below the published 20, with data quality and tuning proposed as untested explanations.
